insights.summary: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹285.45 Cr and profit after tax ₹63.33 Cr (+80% YoY). The order book crossed ₹2,000 Cr, excluding WS Insulators, and the new Sangli coil factory (from 20 Oct) and Turkey PCS plant are operating. The Joint MD left FY27 guidance unchanged until the end of Q3, said Q3 would be 'a kind of a tough time' at the standalone business as production moves between factories, and repeated at least about 50% growth for FY28. The QIP (about ₹700 Cr per an analyst) is targeted for November, with ₹300 Cr earmarked for working capital. This is a concall.in AI-generated transcript.

analyst_questions.answer: Unchanged until the end of Q3. Q3 'tough' at Quality Power because of the factory move; Mehru can improve; Endoks a 'blockbuster year'.
Chips, IGBTs and memory stocked ahead of the Turkey factory (about ₹20 Cr), plus long-lead insulators and bushings at Quality Power and Mehru; 'it will slightly increase over the next few quarters'.

analyst_questions.answer: The Q1 margin was not sustainable (Q4 shipments, vendor drawbacks); aluminium, resin and paint rose. Contracts are fixed price, new ones are signed at higher prices.
95%+ executes in 15-18 months; about 99% fixed price, with a buffer for copper and aluminium moves.

analyst_questions.answer: He did not dispute the figures; orders are paced to capacity because fixed-price orders without capacity 'lose margins'. Larger orders between Q3 and Q4 as capacity comes in.

analyst_questions.answer: Several customers have shaken hands but await financial closure; Quality Power is full with FACTS and HVDC orders and is happy to wait.

red_flags.text: Standalone Q3 is guided to be weak while two factories ramp; customer audits (about 60, one or two a week) run for roughly six months before the new Sangli factory is fully used.
Working capital is rising: inventory has jumped and about ₹300 Cr of the QIP is for working capital, partly because in-house cable adds four months of cash cycle.
PCS orders are booked at only 10-12% margin and the Joint MD says Indian rules (long warranties and guarantees) make the domestic market unsuitable.
Fixed-price orders (about 99%) leave margin exposed to copper, aluminium and resin: standalone material cost rose from 35% to 45% of sales.
Hyperinflation accounting in Turkey swung other expenses (₹8 Cr charge in Q1, ₹4 Cr credit in Q2), so Q2 profit is helped by a one-off.
